key_insight: Joint multilingual training delivered stronger cardiology entity recognition than language-specific models, while specialty pretraining had limited impact on strict F1.
clinical_relevance: CardioLM could support extraction of diseases, symptoms, procedures, and medications from multilingual cardiology documentation.
method: Built CardioCCC from 508 Spanish cardiology case reports, extended to six additional languages through machine translation, annotation projection, and clinician review.
Continued pretraining language-specific encoders on cardiology and biomedical text, then fine-tuned entity recognition models.
Compared language-specific and jointly trained multilingual models using strict and relaxed F1 and clinician ratings.
evidence_signal: Multilingual models exceeded the strongest monolingual system by up to 0.13 strict F1; mean clinician ratings across entity types rose from 26% for a rule-and-dictionary baseline to 73% for CardioNER.
watch_item: Performance on translated case reports may not generalize to native-language clinical records, and entity-boundary errors remained common.
paper_title: CardioLM: A multilingual suite of small language models for the cardiology domain
